# Fixed-source global cut-field averaging and exact response minimax

This is a response-convexification theorem for ONE fixed source, ONE
fixed continuous supporting-slope selection, and hence FIXED contact
sets. The fields are averaged BEFORE constructing the eroded convex
body. This is different from Minkowski averaging the resulting bodies,
whose first cap responses need not average (the exact obstruction is
`candidate d9792f1ce8a8f405`).
No positive game value or OC payment is asserted.

The actual global-cut construction and its radial first variation are
in `candidate 6748c967393345b9`.
Here the first variation is also proved with the uniformity needed
for a compact family of probability mixtures.

## 1. Fixed geometric data and fields

Let d>=1, let P=conv(P) cap Z^n be finite, and let positive compact
convex bodies K_z form an actual compatible family. Put

    C=conv(union_(z in P) {z} times K_z).

Its integer fibers are exactly K_z. All statements may first be made
in aff(P) times R^d; the rational perpendicular thickening from the
global-cut source supplies a full ambient body without altering any
integer fiber when needed.

Fix p in P, y in int K_p, and a continuous feasible supporting slope
A:S^(d-1)->R^n:

    h_z(u)<=h_p(u)+A(u).(z-p).

Write the fixed nonnegative slack

    Delta_z(u)=h_p(u)+A(u).(z-p)-h_z(u)>=0.               (1)

Let Theta be a nonempty compact metric parameter space. For each theta suppose
V_theta(u,z,x) is jointly continuous in(theta,u,z,x), globally finite,
nonnegative, and convex in(z,x) for each fixed(theta,u). It is enough
to have these properties on one common open convex neighborhood of C,
with all cuts intersected with C. Assume the source restriction is
INDEPENDENT of theta:

    V_theta(u,p,x)=Phi_p(u,x) for x in K_p.              (2)

For the projective application Phi_p=H(u)f(1+a.(x-y)), where
H(u)=h_(K_p-y)(u)>0, a is its ordinary projective normalizer, and f is
the globally finite nonnegative convex extension used in that source.
The theorem does not require this special formula except for its
separately cited own-source cap credit.

For any Borel probability nu on Theta set

    V_nu(u,z,x)=integral_Theta V_theta(u,z,x) dnu(theta). (3)

This is continuous, finite, nonnegative and convex in(z,x), and has
exactly the same source restriction. Define the ACTUAL body

    C_e[nu]=C cap intersection_(u in S^(d-1))
       { (z,x):u.x-A(u).(z-p)+e V_nu(u,z,x)<=h_p(u) }.  (4)

Each cut is convex; C_e is compact, convex, and nested in C for e>=0.
Its integer fiber L_z(e;nu) is exactly the intersection of K_z with

    u.x+e V_nu(u,z,x)<=h_z(u)+Delta_z(u) for every u.     (5)

Averaging after(4), or replacing V_nu by a projective field at an
averaged denominator, is NOT the operation being proved here.

## 2. Exact compatibility and uniform positive fibers

Choose o_z+r_z B_d subset K_z, with r_z>0. Joint continuity and compactness
give a common bound M0 for all fields on Theta times S^(d-1) times C.
Every averaged field has the same bound. If t=e M0/r_z<=1, then

    o_z+(1-t)(K_z-o_z) subset L_z(e;nu).                 (6)

Indeed the unperturbed inward support slack of this homothet is at
least t r_z in every direction, which pays e V_nu; the additional
Delta_z is nonnegative. For uniformly small e every integer fiber is
therefore positive. Since C_e contains points above every base in P,
its projection contains conv(P), and it is also contained in C, so its
projection is exactly conv(P). There are no new or deleted integer
bases. Convexity of C_e gives every anchored fiber inclusion exactly,
without a hull repair or a first-order compatibility assumption.

At the source Delta_p(u)=0 for every u. Equations(2),(5) show that its
entire actual erosion is the same for every nu, not just its first
cost. No other source field is present to impose extra source cuts.

## 3. Linear physical speed, including nonsmooth boundaries

At a regular boundary point x of K_z, let u_z(x) be its unique outward
unit normal. Define

    v_theta,z(x)=1_{Delta_z(u_z(x))=0}
                       V_theta(u_z(x),z,x),
    v_nu,z(x)=1_{Delta_z(u_z(x))=0}
                       V_nu(u_z(x),z,x).                (7)

Regularity holds for surface-almost every boundary point. Since the
contact indicator is FIXED, Tonelli gives the pointwise identity

    v_nu,z=integral_Theta v_theta,z dnu(theta)             (8)

almost everywhere. This is the special one-source fact that removes
the contact maximum. It is valid even when the contact set in normal
space has a boundary or the fiber has facets.

Here is the actual radial derivation, not just a formal normal speed.
At an old radial endpoint x write x_t=o_z+(1-t)(x-o_z), and let
t_e(x;nu) be the fractional radial loss of(5). Bound(6) gives
0<=t_e<=e M0/r_z uniformly. If u supports x and Delta_z(u)=0, the new
endpoint satisfies

    t_e u.(x-o_z)>=e V_nu(u,z,x_(t_e)).                  (9)

Conversely, if t_e>0, the new endpoint is interior to K_z and at least
one cut is active. Otherwise compactness of the normal sphere would
give a strictly positive uniform cut slack, contradicting maximality
of the new radial endpoint. An active normal u_e satisfies

    t_e u_e.(x-o_z)
      =e V_nu(u_e,z,x_(t_e))
                 -[h_z(u_e)-u_e.x+Delta_z(u_e)].        (10)

The bracket is nonnegative. Along any convergent sequence of active
normals as e decreases to0 it tends to0, so the limit supports x and
has Delta_z=0. If x is regular this limit is its unique normal. Its
radial support denominator u_z(x).(x-o_z) is at least r_z. Combining
(9),(10) and continuity gives

    t_e(x;nu)/e -> v_nu,z(x)/[u_z(x).(x-o_z)].           (11)

If the unique normal is not a contact normal, a positive radial loss
along any sequence would produce the forbidden contact limit; hence
(11) still holds with zero on its right. If the normal is contact but
its field vanishes, the same upper bound gives zero. Thus all boundary
status cases are included.

Using radial coordinates, the volume element of a fractional shell
over surface point x is

    [u_z(x).(x-o_z)] (1-t)^(d-1) dt dS(x).

The uniform bound(6), regularity almost everywhere and dominated
convergence prove

    |K_z|-|L_z(e;nu)|=e integral_(boundary K_z) v_nu,z dS+o(e). (12)

For d=1 use the two endpoints and counting boundary measure; the same
calculation applies without an exceptional singular set.

For a fixed closed ambient cap H let kappa_z,H be the ACTUAL inward
loss selector: one if K_z is entirely captured, zero if its interior
is disjoint from H, and the indicator of the open cap trace at a
properly cut boundary point. Then

    mu(H)-mu_e[nu](H)
        =e sum_z integral kappa_z,H v_nu,z dS+o(e).      (13)

The cutting hyperplane of a proper cut meets the old convex boundary in
surface measure zero.
At every other old radial endpoint the sufficiently short removed
segment has the same cap status as the endpoint's interior side.
An inside supporting cap captures all loss, an outside supporting cap
captures none, and a pure-base cap uses its exact closed full/empty
fiber trace. Thus a supporting facet is not assigned its closed
indicator as a fictitious outside loss.

## 4. Uniform first variations for every probability mixture

The errors in(12),(13) are uniform over ALL Borel probabilities nu on
Theta, for any fixed finite cap menu. Here are the compactness details.
The parameter-to-field map restricted to S^(d-1) times C is continuous
in the uniform norm. The barycenter map nu->V_nu on this compact set
is continuous from weak probability convergence to uniform convergence:
pointwise convergence follows from the definition of weak convergence;
a finite domain net and the uniform continuity of the original joint
field make that convergence uniform. Hence the family of averaged
fields is compact in the uniform norm and uniformly bounded.

If uniform first variation failed, choose e_j decreasing to0 and nu_j
witnessing that failure, then pass to a subsequence for which V_(nu_j)
converges uniformly to a field V_nu. At each regular x the argument
(9)--(11) works verbatim along this sequence: the field evaluations
converge uniformly, and every limiting active normal must be the same
old contact normal. It follows that

 t_(e_j)(x;nu_j)/e_j
    -v_(nu_j),z(x)/[u_z(x).(x-o_z)] ->0.

Bound(6) dominates these differences. For proper cap selectors discard
also their surface-null boundary intersections. The same dominated
convergence proves the integrated differences tend to0, contradicting
the selected failure. This proves uniformity without assuming a smooth
support function, differentiable dependence on theta, or uniform
convergence of the normal contact indicators. Those indicators do not
vary in this theorem.

## 5. Exact response convex hull and finite-menu minimax

Let H_1,...,H_m be any fixed finite closed ambient caps, and fix a number
beta. For a pure parameter theta define

    D(theta)=sum_z integral v_theta,z dS,
    C_j(theta)=sum_z integral kappa_z,H_j v_theta,z dS,
    R_j(theta)=C_j(theta)-beta D(theta).                 (14)

All these functions are continuous on Theta: uniform convergence of
the fields and the fixed bounded measurable contact/cap selectors
bound each response difference by total boundary area times the field
supremum difference. Equations(8),(12),(13) prove EXACT first-response
linearity:

    (D,C_1,...,C_m)(nu)=integral (D,C_1,...,C_m)(theta)dnu,
    R(nu)=integral R(theta)dnu.                         (15)

Thus the set of attainable signed response vectors is precisely the
compact convex hull of R(Theta). Every such vector is realized by one
actual deformation(4), and by a finite mixture of at most m+1 fields,
by finite-dimensional Caratheodory. If total cost and every separate
cap response must also be retained as coordinates, at most m+2 fields
suffice. This is equality of physical first-response sets, not merely
an upper relaxation of them.

The exact finite-menu game value is

    v*=max_nu min_j R_j(nu)
      =min_{lambda_j>=0, sum lambda=1}
                         max_(theta in Theta) sum_j lambda_j R_j(theta). (16)

For a direct separation proof, let K=conv R(Theta). Its attained max
of min_j r_j is v*. The compact convex K is disjoint from the open
orthant(v*,infinity)^m. A separating vector must have nonnegative
coordinates, since that orthant is unbounded in every positive
coordinate. Normalize its sum to1. It gives sup_(r in K)lambda.r<=v*.
Conversely every such lambda has lambda.r>=min_j r_j for every r, so
its support value is at least v*. This proves(16) with attainment.

In particular a mixture makes EVERY selected signed response strictly
positive iff v*>0, equivalently iff every probability vector lambda
admits a parameter theta with sum lambda_j R_j(theta)>0. Compactness
and continuity make the last condition uniformly positive after
minimizing over lambda. No assertion that this condition always holds
is included.

For the usual application suppose a finite fixed closed cap family
covers the old mixed body, critical rows have mu(H_j)=beta M, and all
other covering rows satisfy mu(H_j)<beta M with fixed strict slack. If the critical
rows satisfy R_j(nu)>0, then(12)--(15) give

    mu_e[nu](H_j)/M_e[nu]
                  =beta-e R_j(nu)/M+o(e)<beta.

Slack rows persist, and the new body is a subset of the old one, so
its same fixed cap cover proves strict global normalized descent.
This last conclusion needs the stated actual cover and positive game
value; averaging alone supplies neither.

## 6. Denominator shifts and clipped affine support tilts

The following root-supplied family meets the theorem's hypotheses.
Keep the optimal source a, H, and globally finite nonnegative convex f
fixed. Let b_theta(u),c_theta(u) be jointly continuous on the compact
parameter space times the unit sphere. Put

 V_theta(u,z,x)=max{
     H(u) f(1+a.(x-y)+b_theta(u).(z-p))
                         -c_theta(u).(z-p), 0}.         (17)

For fixed(theta,u), the expression inside braces is convex in the
FULL real variables(z,x), and taking its maximum with zero preserves
convexity and nonnegativity. Joint continuity and boundedness on
compact C hold. At z=p the affine correction vanishes and every
parameter gives exactly H(u)f(1+a.(x-y)), so(2) holds.

Formula(17) allows denominator shifts and a clipped affine support-plane
tilt while retaining the ORIGINAL fixed feasible slope A and therefore
the same contact sets. On the branch where the brace is positive,
its affine correction algebraically replaces A by A+e c_theta inside
the perturbed inequality; no feasibility of that new unperturbed slope
is assumed or needed. The maximum with zero keeps the actual erosion
nested. The admissibility and exact response convexification hold for
these fields, including finite mixtures and compact probability mixtures.
No normal-cost bound or automatic critical-cap credit beyond the fixed
source's prescribed projective credit is claimed.

## 7. Limits of this linearization

- Varying the feasible supporting slope A changes Delta and its contact
  set. The fixed-contact proof does not then apply.
- With several independently imposed sources, the physical boundary
  speed is the MAXIMUM of their active field values. Averaging each
  source field separately does not generally average that maximum.
- Minkowski interpolation of the resulting convex bodies is a different
  operation and has the archived exact nonlinear cap-response obstruction.
- Averages of inverse-power fields are permitted convex cut fields;
  they need not be a single inverse-power field with an averaged b.
- Infinite noncompact parameter menus require separate boundedness,
  continuity and attainment arguments; (16) is asserted here only for
  finite menus or the stated compact continuous parameter family.

Accordingly this theorem legitimizes one concrete finite-menu minimax
on ACTUAL shape responses. Its geometric value remains a separate
inequality, not an unproved consequence of response convexity.
